newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports News - April 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports News - April 7.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

After Australia secured a semi final berth in the Davis Cup tennis on Saturday, the team's celebrations that night, saw players Pat Rafter and Mark Philippoussis fronting up to the reverse singles matches on Sunday admitting they were hungover, and for Rafter, still "sobering up" through his match. Page 25.

While the Queensland Reds rugby union Super 12 team may have an impressive line up of names, such as Tim Horan, Ben Tune, Jason Little and John Eales, the team's first win in the competition against Otago was not at all persuasive. It would seem the side is not yet playing as a team as the Reds finished with a 37-24 win after a half-time score of 31-10. Page 26.

Australian basketballer Shane Heal may be a Minnesota Timberwolf in paypacket only in the U.S. NBA, as he is so far down the team's reserve bench he may never play. Heal has yet to show he is point-scorer or a guard at this level of the game. Page 29.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

The Super 12 rugby union match at the Sydney Football Stadium on Sunday was played before a crowd of 26,245 people, with the New South Wales Waratahs defeating South Africa's Northern Transvaal 43-29. However, the Waratahs' victory was marred by flaws, with both teams showing poor form. Page 21.

Queensland surfer Trudy Todd edged out world champion Pam Burridge to win the A$20,000 Clearwater Classic at Manly yesterday. Todd, who was suffering the flu and had to compete in difficult, low-tide waves, showed speed and power to overcome her taller rvals. Page 23.

Tom Maher, the coach of the Opals, Australia's women's basketball team, described his team's performance as beautiful, as it defeated Japan 99-67 to win all four matches in the international series. While the Opals won by a large margin, they were only ahead by six points at half time, and faced spirited competition from the Japanese. Page 26.
THE AGE

Stan Alves, the coach of Australian Football League team St Kilda, is under pressure to resign after it was revealed yesterday some senior players expressed doubt about him continuing to coach the team in 1997. St Kilda has lost both its matches this seaon, including a 97 point loss to Brisbane yesterday. Page S3.

It is believed Ian Healy and Geoff Marsh, the co-selectors of the Australian cricket team in South Africa, are keen for captain Mark Taylor to sit out the rest of the tour in South Africa, given Mark Waugh's return from injury, and the impressive form of his replacement Adam Gilchrist. Page S2.

Injury troubles have hit Australian Football League club Essendon, with Paul Barnard and Dean Wallis out of the match against North Melbourne next Sunday at the Melbourne Cricket Ground, and James Hird in some doubt after yesterday's 33 point win over Port Adelaide. Page S3.
THE HERALD SUN

Officials from the Sydney Swans Australian Football League club were seething last night over tagging tactics employed by the Western Bulldogs that they said left captain Paul Kelly covered in scratches and bruises. Kelly was forced from the field twice uring Saturday's game under the blood rule. Page 88.

The Gold Coast Indy Car race turned into a crashfest yesterday, with Christian Fittipaldi transported to hospital after an accident involving Gil de Ferran and Gualter Salles. As more than 12 cars retired in the 28-car field after accidents or mechanical failures, Scott Pruett was able to avoid the many collisions and win the race. Page 86.

Soccer player Bill Damianos assisted South Melbourne in their 1-0 win against West Adelaide in the Ericsson Cup yesterday. Damianos was axed from the South Melbourne squad last week after Carlton announced it had signed him for next season, yet the player tore up the contract with Carlton and has now signed to play with South Melbourne for another three years. Page 80.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Draft legislation to be introduced during the autumn session of the New South Wales Parliament this month may allow Sydney race clubs to race as often as they wish on Sundays. Gaming and Racing Minister Richard Face said the only proviso was that additional race dates do not add to the turf calendar. Page 27.

Parramatta rugby league coach Brian Smith admitted yesterday the team needed to be totally rebuilt, despite its A$9 million player splurge last year. The team lost 29-10 to the Newcastle Knights yesterday, with it struggling for control of the ball with ittle pressure from the Knights. Page 31.

Both coaches of the Illawarra and South Queensland rugby league teams said yesterday the match between the two teams, which Illawarra won 14-6, was one of the worst of the decade. Illawarra coach Andrew Farrar said if he had his way he would refund the mney paid by the 6000-strong crowd. Page 32.
